# A voice session, appended to the ISP1 one by src/omci/drv-test.sh with
# OMCI_POTS_PORTS on: what an OLT that offers SIP over OMCI builds for the
# voice path, in the order G.988 Figure 9.9-1 suggests. Unlike the ISP
# sessions this is not from a log: no line provisions voice, so it is
# written by hand, one entity per line, every value made up. The voice rides
# on IP host 1 in a bridge of its own (2), with one GEM port (1600, on
# T-CONT 0x8000) that admits VID 200, and a class 171 instance on the IP
# host that tags its untagged frames with VLAN 200, priority 5. The SIP
# agent comes last, after the bridge port: its TCP/UDP pointer is what
# makes IP host 1 the voice one.
#
# 0c00: Set 138/0: SIP (attribute 2), configured over OMCI (4)
# 0c01: Set 134/1, the IP host of the voice: DHCP on
# 0c02: Create 45/2: the voice bridge, as ISP1 creates its own
# 0c03: Create 268/0x10: GEM port 1600 on T-CONT 0x8000, both ways, queue 0x8005
# 0c04: Create 266/0x10: its IW TP, MAC bridged, on bridge 2
# 0c05: Create 47/0x10: bridge 2 port 1, TP type 4, IP host 1
# 0c06: Create 47/0x11: bridge 2 port 2, TP type 5, the GEM IW TP
# 0c07: Create 84/0x11: VID 200 only on the GEM side (FwdOp 0x10, one entry)
# 0c08: Create 171/0x20: association type 3, IP host 1
# 0c09: Set 171/0x20: input and output TPID 0x8100, downstream mode 0 (inverse)
# 0c0a: Set 171/0x20: untagged frames get C-VID 200 priority 5
# 0c0b: Create 136/1: SIP over UDP 5060 on IP host 1
# 0c0c: Create 150/1: the SIP agent (no servers named here)
# 0c0d: Set 150/1: its TCP/UDP pointer, 136/1: IP host 1 is the voice one
